core_message: Juliane Koepcke survived a 3 km fall in her seat after her plane broke up over the Amazon, then walked out of the rainforest using what her biologist father taught her.
title: She Fell 3 km From a Plane and Lived
description:
On 24 December 1971, LANSA Flight 508, a Lockheed L-188 Electra flying from Lima to Pucallpa, Peru, entered a thunderstorm, was struck by lightning and broke up in the air. Seventeen-year-old Juliane Koepcke fell about 3 km into the rainforest still strapped into her row of seats. She woke with a broken collarbone, a deep cut and concussion. Her parents were biologists who ran a research station in the forest, and she remembered her father's advice to follow water downhill. She walked and waded downstream for days until she found a loggers' shelter, where she was found on her eleventh day in the forest and taken to safety. Of the 92 people on board, she was the only survivor; her mother, the ornithologist Maria Koepcke, was among those who died. Juliane later became a biologist herself.

Source: Wikipedia, LANSA Flight 508; Wikipedia, Juliane Koepcke.

scenes.narration: On Christmas Eve 1971, a seventeen-year-old girl fell three kilometres into the Amazon rainforest, still strapped into her seat. She survived.
Juliane Koepcke was flying with her mother over Peru when their plane flew into a thunderstorm. Lightning struck it, and it broke apart in the air.
She woke up alone on the forest floor with a broken collarbone. Her parents were biologists, and her father had taught her: if you're lost, follow water downstream.
So she walked and waded down creeks and rivers for days, until she found a loggers' hut on the bank.
On her eleventh day in the forest, the loggers found her. She was the only one of ninety-two people on board to survive.
